## The problem

Our team of twelve has drifted into long-lived feature branches that often survive a week or more before merging. Merges have become dreaded events: conflicts pile up, integration bugs surface late, and code review happens on a diff so large that reviewers rubber-stamp it rather than truly engage. We ship less predictably because "almost done" work sits invisible on a branch until it collides with everyone else's changes at the last minute.

## The proposal

I propose we move to trunk-based development: everyone commits small, reviewed changes directly to main at least daily, guarded by feature flags for anything incomplete.

- Branches live no more than a day or two before merging, keeping diffs small and reviewable.
- Incomplete or risky features ship behind flags, decoupling "merged" from "released."
- CI must stay green on main at all times, with a fast rollback path for any breakage.
- Pull requests shrink dramatically, so review turns around in hours, not days.
- We adopt a lightweight branching policy doc so expectations are explicit from day one.

This isn't a process for its own sake — it directly targets the integration pain and review fatigue described above.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real: trunk-based development demands stronger test coverage and CI discipline than we currently have, and without that safety net, frequent merges to main could destabilize it rather than stabilize it. If our test suite has gaps, we could be trading rare, painful merge conflicts for frequent, quieter production regressions — arguably a worse trade. I take this seriously rather than waving it away: we should invest two to three weeks up front hardening CI and closing critical coverage gaps before we fully cut over, and treat that investment as a prerequisite, not an afterthought.

There's also a cultural risk — engineers accustomed to long branches may feel pressure to ship unfinished work. Feature flags address this directly by letting code merge without being user-facing.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
